title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Asha Menon
description: Context: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatibility layer for /v1/chat.completions to parity with upstream behavior for parameters, role semantics, stop sequences and logprobs, and tidy up response formatting and streaming stability. Motivation: customers using OpenAI-compatible clients expect identical behavior when migrating. Changes include mapping of legacy params (temperature, top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty), deterministic role handling for system/user/assistant roles, correct propagation of stop tokens through streaming and KV cache, accurate logprobs in both streaming and non-streaming modes, and consistent JSON/structured output formatting. This PR touches the compatibility adapter, API layer, streaming muxer, and test harness; includes unit and integration tests and release notes. Checklist: [x] param mapping implemented, [x] role normalization and validation, [x] stop token propagation for streaming, [x] logprobs surface parity, [x] response formatting fixes, [x] tests and regression evals, [x] docs updated. Related: Linear ENG-2345, ENG-2389. Notes: attempted to avoid breaking changes by keeping Redwood-native defaults when OpenAI fields are absent. See comments below for follow-ups around debug logging and a follow-up perf tweak for batching (ENG-2422).
commits: a7f3c12: compatibility: map OpenAI generation params to internal config
d4e8b91: runtime: normalize roles early in request pipeline

review_comments: Carlos Rivera (2026-02-20): Thanks for the thorough PR. A few nits: prefer explicit nil checks in params_mapping.go to avoid accidental zero-value overrides; also add a small test for empty stop array behavior.
Asha Menon (2026-02-20): Addressed the nil checks and added the empty stop array test. PTAL.

Emily Zhang (2026-02-22): Verified logprobs numbers against the reference harness. Numbers match within tolerance. One question: streaming chunk boundaries currently recompute token offsets; please ensure offsets are stable across reconnections.
Asha Menon (2026-02-22): Added stable offset tracking in muxer.go and a regression test that simulates reconnects.
